disclaimer_en: Orbit supports decisions; it does not diagnose. Values marked team_criterion are design choices pending validation.

baseline.note: Pre-flight baseline, recalculated once stable in flight (team criterion). For the demo, read persona.baseline.

convergence.evidence_en: On the ISS, sleep under 6 h was associated with slower psychomotor speed, more stress and higher workload (Jones et al., 2022).

green.en: Keep going. Your protective factors are working.

yellow.en: Self-care suggestion. Orbit checks again in 24 h.

early_signal.en: Early signal across body, mind or crew. Choose up to two actions.

red_physical.en: This needs a person. Your crew medical officer has been notified.

red_psych.en: You asked to talk to someone today. Who would you like?

indicators.rule_en: Yellow: under 7 h and more than 1 h below baseline. Red: 5 h or less for 3 nights in a row.
indicators.action_en: Protect tonight's sleep window and light schedule. Red: crew medical officer.
indicators.hrp_risk: Risk of Inadequate Sleep and Irregular Schedules
indicators.why_en: Sleep is the lever that touches mood, reaction time and immunity. Orbit compares each night with your own usual range, not with Earth averages.

indicators.red: self_triggered: astronaut taps 'I want to talk to someone today' and chooses who
indicators.rule_en: Yellow: any item 2 points or more worse than baseline. Red: only when she asks to talk to someone today.
indicators.action_en: Boost options she chooses. Red: she picks the crew medical officer or an earlier private psychological conference.
indicators.hrp_risk: Risk of Behavioral Changes and Psychiatric Disorders
indicators.why_en: A dip can be a normal reaction to a hard week. Orbit only flags it when it lasts and shows up together with other signals.

indicators.rule_en: Yellow: 2 points or more below baseline.
indicators.action_en: Suggest a crew activity or a private note; nothing is shared by default.
indicators.why_en: How the crew feels together matters on long missions. Only you see this rating unless you choose to share it.

indicators.rule_en: Yellow: 3 or more on either scale (positive screen, not a diagnosis). No red: after two weeks, Orbit offers an earlier private conference.
indicators.action_en: Offer a private conversation; share with the medical officer only if she agrees.
indicators.hrp_risk: Risk of Behavioral Changes and Psychiatric Disorders
indicators.why_en: These are widely used two-question checks. A high score is not a diagnosis; it means it is worth talking to someone.

indicators.rule_en: Yellow: median reaction time slower than baseline + 2 SD in 2 of the last 3 sessions. Never red on its own.
indicators.action_en: Check sleep and workload; counts toward the cross-domain signal.
indicators.hrp_risk: Risk of Behavioral Changes and Psychiatric Disorders

sources.cite: Jones et al., 2022 (PVT-B on the ISS)

indicators.why_en: A 3-minute check of your alertness against your own best days. It is not a test of your abilities and never raises an alarm by itself.
indicators.note_en: PVT-B-style task; our implementation is not a validated PVT-B.

indicators.rule_en: Green: under 120/80. Yellow: 120-129 systolic, or 130-139 / 80-89. Red: 140 or more, or 90 or more, confirmed on a second reading.
indicators.action_en: Repeat and review sleep, exercise and salt. Red: crew medical officer.
indicators.why_en: One high reading is repeated before it counts. Orbit shows your trend so you and your medical officer see the pattern.

indicators.input: watch or biometric shirt on waking
indicators.rule_en: Yellow: 10 bpm or more above baseline. Red: over 100 at rest repeatedly, or under 60 with dizziness or fainting.
indicators.action_en: Check sleep, stress and hydration. Red: crew medical officer.
indicators.why_en: Your resting heart rate rises with poor sleep, stress or illness. Orbit compares it with your own normal, which may be lower than average.

indicators.input: same method every day, on waking
indicators.rule_en: Yellow: more than 0.5 °C above in-flight baseline. Red: 38 °C or more, more than 0.5 °C above in-flight baseline, with symptoms.
indicators.action_en: Fluids, rest and log symptoms. Red: crew medical officer.
indicators.hrp_risk: Risk of Altered Immune System Responses
indicators.why_en: On long missions your body runs about 1 °C warmer than on Earth. Orbit uses your in-flight normal so it does not raise false fevers.

indicators.rule_en: Green: 70-99. Yellow: 100-125, or 54-69 (level 1 hypoglycemia). Red: 126 or more on two occasions, or under 54 (level 2).
indicators.action_en: Review food and exercise. Red: crew medical officer.
indicators.hrp_risk: Risk of Inadequate Food and Nutrition

sources.cite: ADA Standards of Care, section 6 (hypoglycemia levels; 2025 version reviewed)

indicators.why_en: Fasting glucose shows how your body handles energy. Insulin resistance has risen in flight studies, so Orbit tracks your trend.

indicators.rule_en: Yellow: under 75 % of today's prescription. Never red on its own.
indicators.action_en: Reschedule the session; linked to mood.
indicators.hrp_risk: Risk of Reduced Cardiorespiratory and Musculoskeletal Fitness
indicators.why_en: Exercise protects bone, heart and mood. Orbit counts what you did against your plan and never shames a missed day.

indicators.rule_en: Yellow: 3 days in a row without contact, or a drop of 50 % or more versus the previous 14 days. Never red on its own.
indicators.action_en: Suggest an asynchronous message or the family puzzle.
indicators.hrp_risk: Risk of Behavioral Changes and Psychiatric Disorders
indicators.why_en: Talking less with Earth is common on long missions. Orbit notices the trend so you can choose when to reconnect.

indicators.rule_en: Yellow: a symptom lasting more than 2 days. Red: any red-flag symptom (list pending review by a physician).
indicators.action_en: Log it. Red: crew medical officer immediately.
indicators.hrp_risk: Risk of Altered Immune System Responses; Risk of Spaceflight Associated Neuro-ocular Syndrome (SANS); Risk of Cardiovascular Adaptations

sources.cite: Mayo Clinic, Tachycardia (chest pain, shortness of breath, weakness: seek immediate help)

indicators.why_en: Tap where you feel something. Some symptoms go straight to your medical officer because they need a person, not an app.

indicators.input: scenario dose rate + DONKI solar particle events
indicators.rule_en: Yellow: a solar particle event is active. No red in the app; shelter is an operational decision.
indicators.why_en: This is your mission's estimated dose and solar activity, from NASA data. Shelter decisions belong to crew procedures, not to Orbit.

indicators.rule_en: No color: it is a tank that fills up.
indicators.hrp_risk: Risk of Behavioral Changes and Psychiatric Disorders
indicators.why_en: These are the things that keep you well. Orbit counts them so you can see what works for you.

changes_0_2: Pulse mode: 3-minute PVT-B-style task (approved 16:54). Engine parameter names kept from v0.1; new keys only add task settings
Symptoms: 'shortness of breath' added to red_flags
Boost content lives in boost-cards.json (P0) and orbit-boost-library.json (triggers and safety flow)
